Maintenance Report — MNT-0051-025

Asset: WELL-0051 (SW-24 Well 051, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 12 Apr 2025 08:00 · Finished: 23 Apr 2025 09:00 · Well stopped for this job: 265 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Brian Coleman Triggered by: inspection INS-0051-0128 on 2025-04-10 Report written: 24 Apr 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that the pump jack was running rough with a loud knock at the top of each stroke, so the operator stopped it. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0051-0128 showed the wellhead at 24.0 °C with the air at 18.4 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing. The well stayed shut in for about 9 days longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

Root cause

Bearing wear from long service and an overdue grease interval. This is corrective repair number 4 on this well's pump jack in the last 12 months.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
  2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
  3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
  4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
  5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.

Asset: WELL-0051 (SW-24 Well 051, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: flowline Work started: 23 May 2025 08:00 · Finished: 24 May 2025 12:00 · Well stopped for this job: 28 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Brian Coleman, Kevin Price Triggered by: inspection INS-0051-0133 on 2025-05-22 Report written: 25 May 2025

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0051-0133 at 07:45 on 2025-05-22 found crude oil on the pad: about 0.8% of the pad area, estimated 0.3 bbl. The inspector noted: "Oil sheen around cellar." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 1.8 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to the flanged flowline connection at the wellhead cellar.

Root cause

A failed gasket on the flange where the flowline leaves the wellhead. This is corrective repair number 3 on this well's flowline in the last 12 months.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 5 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Cleaned free oil out of the cellar.
  2. Unbolted the flange and removed the failed gasket.
  3. Fitted a new gasket and new bolts, torqued to specification.
  4. Excavated the stained soil around the cellar.

Summary of the fix: replaced the flange gasket and bolts and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 284 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 227 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.
